primaryAudience: finance director at a regional cooperative
viewerDecision: whether to run a four-week pilot of one shared ledger
primaryTakeaway: Move the monthly close onto one shared ledger.

nextStep.action: Agree a four-week pilot with two teams

audioDirection.pauses: hold each number for a beat

limitations: Fictional example for planning. Every name and figure is invented.

narrative.problem: the monthly close runs on five spreadsheets that disagree
narrative.solution: Larkspur Close keeps one ledger every team posts to
narrative.ask: agree a four-week pilot with two teams

beats.narration: Move the monthly close onto one shared ledger.
Five spreadsheets feed the close, and they rarely agree. Reviewers spend the last days reconciling, not reviewing.
beats.actionTitle: Disagreeing spreadsheets push the close into its last days.
beats.supportingArgument: The reviewers spend their time on matching numbers.

evidenceClaims.text: The close draws on five spreadsheets that must be matched by hand.

beats.narration: A four-day close ties up reviewers for twice as long as a two-day close.
beats.actionTitle: Every late close day costs reviewer time we can measure.
beats.supportingArgument: The cost grows each month the close stays manual.

measurement.comparison: 2 days to close after one team moved to a shared ledger
measurement.method: time sheets compared before and after

beats.narration: Larkspur Close keeps one ledger. Teams post once, and reviewers read the same entries.
beats.actionTitle: Larkspur Close gives every team one ledger to post to.
beats.supportingArgument: One ledger removes the matching step.

evidenceClaims.text: Teams post to one shared ledger and reviewers read the same entries.

beats.narration: A similar cooperative cut its close from four days to two in one quarter.
beats.actionTitle: A comparable cooperative halved its close time in a quarter.
beats.supportingArgument: A like-for-like case shows the result is reachable.

evidenceClaims.text: Close time fell from four days to two.

measurement.method: close calendar compared before and after

beats.narration: Start with one team, two teams, or the whole group. We suggest two teams.
beats.actionTitle: Starting with two teams balances speed and risk.
beats.supportingArgument: Three starting points let you pick your own pace.

beats.narration: Agree a four-week pilot with two teams by the first of next month.
